analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts and the complete bounded patch for SSDPrefixCache.swift. The only changes add optional unusedSince to retireOwnedEntries/retireIndexedEntries (HEAD 1790–1794) and forward it to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove (HEAD 1799–1800). No concrete regression is established by this forwarding change alone. Existing staging authenticates model/layout/full lookup-tag bindings, checks cancellation and epochs, and balances provisional/shared reservations (BASE 1291–1592, 1723–1753). Startup recovery checks safe paths and bindings before indexing (1865–1966); durable-ready reporting reauthenticates surviving blocks and retains conservative recompute bounds (2052–2133). These surrounding paths are unchanged, as are scope hashing, encryption calls and sliding-TTL behavior relevant to T-041, A-001 and TB-007. No changed authorization, attestation, credential, billing or privileged-helper behavior is visible.
Integration must examine the new unusedSince predicate in SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove and its changed callers: which clock/cutoff supplies it, whether nil preserves unconditional retirement, and whether freshness is revalidated against concurrent index.touch/file-mtime updates (BASE 1578–1586) under appropriate synchronization. These implementations are outside the supplied units; their absence is not evidence of a missing control. The remaining question is whether the combined change preserves TTL/LRU cleanup and coherent disk accounting without deleting recently used entries or retaining expired entries unexpectedly.
